notes: cmd/runtime-proxy/mcp.go:295-297 and cmd/runtime-proxy/approvalscan_test.go:79-81 (and the commit message) state a falsehood about the prior behaviour: 'the old order had one thing going for it: a call the scanner refuses never became an approval request'. Under the old order the gate ran first, so a scanner-refused call DID create an approval request — I verified this by restoring main's mcp.go and running the new tests, which failed with 'a refused call created 1 approval requests'. That property is newly introduced by this PR, not preserved from the old order. The comments describe the new code correctly; only the historical framing is wrong. Rationale-comment inaccuracy in a security-critical file, no behavioural impact.

Test validity checked empirically: with main's cmd/runtime-proxy/mcp.go restored, TestAGatedCallIsScannedBeforeAReviewerIsAsked and TestACallTheScannerRefusesNeverBecomesAnApproval both fail, and pass on HEAD — they genuinely exercise the change. TestACleanGatedCallReachesTheReviewerUnchanged passes on the pre-fix code too; it is a no-regression guard rather than a regression test, which is fine but worth knowing.

Fail-closed ordering verified: replaceArguments (mcp.go:440) unmarshals the replacement before it is assigned to request.Params.Arguments (mcp.go:322), so the gate can never be handed non-JSON; a replacement that will not parse takes the -32006 block path. The body sent upstream after approval is the same rewritten body.

No residual leak through the reviewer excerpt: trimArguments truncates to 2000 bytes (approval.go:197) while the DLP scan limit is 256 KiB (internal/dlp/dlp.go:127), so everything the reviewer is shown lies inside the scanned prefix. dlp.Scan carries the tail past the limit through unchanged, so the body rewrite does not truncate a long payload.

Undocumented user-visible behaviour change: docs/user-guide.md:569 tells reviewers they see '어떤 인자로 호출하려는지'; gated calls now show DLP-redacted arguments. The doc is not wrong (what is shown is what is sent) but the redaction is not mentioned anywhere in the guide.

Pre-existing and untouched by this PR, but adjacent: if the strict json.Unmarshal at mcp.go:270 fails, methodAndTool (mcp.go:155) recovers the method and tool name but not the arguments, so request.Params.Arguments stays empty, the argument scan at mcp.go:298 is skipped by its len>0 guard, and the body still goes upstream. Same class of bypass as the batch/Content-Encoding holes already closed above it; arguments are not recovered leniently the way method and tool are.

Scope: the BASE_VERSION 0.25.0 -> 0.26.0 bump and its four call sites (compose.yaml, README.md, deploy/kubernetes/ollama-bridge.yaml, internal/buildinfo) follow this repo's established convention — Dockerfile.base:8 builds cmd/runtime-proxy into the base image, and 9f84183 and bd7f2ae bumped it the same way for the same directory. Not scope creep. No stale 0.25.0 references remain outside node_modules.
Verification run: go build ./... clean, go vet ./cmd/runtime-proxy clean, go test ./cmd/runtime-proxy -race -count=1 passes, and the full go test ./... -count=1 suite passes with no failures.

Revert safety: code plus version-string changes only, no migration or external state. A revert would put BASE_VERSION back to 0.25.0 after an agenthub-base:v0.26.0 image may have been published, which is the same mild awkwardness every prior base-version bump in this series carries.
